def page() -> None:
    """The ready banner on top, then two tabs: the settings with the day and the
    network, and the day profiles."""
    s = services()
    scenario = s.scenario.current()
    with shell(
        "summary",
        "Summary",
        "The market as configured: every setting once, the day's curves and the "
        "network. Change settings on their own pages, then run it on Step.",
    ):
        check_box = ui.column().classes("w-full")
        with ui.tabs().classes("w-full").props("align=left no-caps") as tabs:
            settings_tab = ui.tab("Settings", icon="fact_check")
            profiles_tab = ui.tab("Day profiles", icon="show_chart")
        with ui.tab_panels(tabs, value=settings_tab).classes("w-full bg-transparent"):
            with ui.tab_panel(settings_tab).classes("p-0 gap-4"):
                with ui.row().classes("w-full gap-4 items-stretch no-wrap"):
                    with section("Network and day", icon="hub", classes="grow basis-0"):
                        _grid(scenario)
                    with section("Market", icon="gavel", classes="grow basis-0"):
                        _market(scenario)
                    with section("DSO", icon="account_balance", classes="grow basis-0"):
                        _dso(scenario)
                with section("Participants", icon="groups"):
                    _participants(scenario)
                with ui.row().classes("w-full gap-4 items-stretch no-wrap"):
                    with section(
                        "Participants over the day",
                        "Their summed demand and generation per step; every "
                        "curve is in the Day profiles tab",
                        "show_chart",
                        classes="grow basis-0",
                    ):
                        day_box = ui.column().classes("w-full")
                    with section(
                        "Network",
                        "Rings: the participants",
                        "hub",
                        classes="grow basis-0",
                    ):
                        network_box = ui.column().classes("w-full")
            with ui.tab_panel(profiles_tab).classes("p-0 gap-4"):
                profiles_box = ui.column().classes("w-full gap-4")

    async def load() -> None:
        _checks(check_box, scenario, None)
        if not scenario.participants:
            for box in (day_box, network_box):
                box.clear()
            with profiles_box:
                placeholder(
                    "No participants yet. Place them on the Grid & Participants "
                    "page to see their day.",
                    "groups",
                )
            return
        for box in (day_box, profiles_box):
            busy(box, "Reading the profiles …")
        busy(network_box, "Building topology …")
        try:
            day = await run.io_bound(s.profiles.day_profiles, scenario)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  show the error on the page
            for box in (day_box, profiles_box, network_box):
                failed(box, e)
            return
        day_box.clear()
        with day_box:
            ui.plotly(day_figure(day, day.owned())).classes("w-full")
        profiles_box.clear()
        with profiles_box:
            show_day_profiles(day, scenario)
        _checks(check_box, scenario, day)
        try:
            topology = await run.io_bound(
                s.grid.topology, NetworkRef("simbench", scenario.grid.code)
            )
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  show the error on the page
            failed(network_box, e)
            return
        network_box.clear()
        with network_box:
            marked = {p.bus for p in scenario.participants}
            ui.plotly(topology_figure(topology, highlight=marked, height=300)).classes(
                "w-full"
            )

    ui.timer(0.05, load, once=True)

    """Register the pages and start the server.

def shell(active: str, title: str, subtitle: str = "") -> Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Build the page frame; the caller fills the content inside the `with` block."""
    apply_theme()
    dark = ui.dark_mode(value=app.storage.user.get("dark", False))

    # Left navigation (NAV in navigation.py); the current page is highlighted.
    with ui.left_drawer(value=True, bordered=True).props("width=232").classes(
        "mls-drawer q-pt-sm"
    ) as drawer:
        for group, items in NAV:
            if group:
                ui.label(group).classes("mls-nav-group")
            else:
                ui.element("div").classes("q-mt-sm")
            for item in items:
                is_active = item.key == active
                with ui.item(on_click=lambda r=item.route: ui.navigate.to(r)).props(
                    "dense"
                ).classes("mls-nav-item" + (" mls-nav-active" if is_active else "")):
                    with ui.item_section().props("avatar").style("min-width: 34px"):
                        ui.icon(item.icon, size="20px")
                    with ui.item_section():
                        ui.item_label(item.label)

    with ui.header(elevated=False).classes("mls-header items-center q-px-md gap-3"):
        ui.button(icon="menu", on_click=drawer.toggle).props(
            "flat round dense color=white"

        ui.icon("bolt", size="26px").classes("text-amber-4")
        ui.label("MARLEM Studio").classes("mls-brand")
        ui.space()
        _scenario_button()
        ui.button(icon="dark_mode", on_click=lambda: _toggle_dark(dark)).props(
            "flat round dense color=white"

    # Page heading; the page's own content follows where the caller's
    # `with shell(...)` block continues (the yield).
    with ui.column().classes("mls-page w-full"):
        with ui.column().classes("gap-0"):
            ui.label(title).classes("mls-title")
            if subtitle:
                ui.label(subtitle).classes("mls-subtitle")
        yield

docs.title: probes
docs.text:
core.rl.envs.probes · source on GitHub

Probe environments: tiny tasks whose correct value and policy are known exactly.

After Andy Jones, "Debugging RL, Without the Agonizing Pain" (https://andyljones.com/posts/rl-debugging.html): a sequence of environments, each adding one piece of the learning problem, so the first one that fails names the broken piece. Here they are multi-agent and continuous (Box(-1, 1) observations and actions, like the market), and each agent has its own reward, so they also check what the training paradigms add: routing every agent's observation, action and reward to the right place, and summing rewards for the grouped paradigms (CTCE, CTDE).

1  ConstantProbe       value       obs 0, reward +1             V = 1
2  ObservationProbe    obs -> value  obs ±1, reward = obs       V(o) = o
3  DiscountProbe       discounting  obs 0 then 1, +1 at the end  V(0) = γ, V(1) = 1
4  ActionProbe         policy      obs 0, reward peaks at t_i    action = t_i
5  ObsActionProbe      obs -> policy  obs ±1, reward peaks at o/2  action = o/2

Each agent has a different target t_i in probe 4, so an action delivered to the wrong agent shows. scramble_ids names the agents so that their sorted order differs from their order in the environment (GroupedEnv sorts the agents' spaces; RLlib groups their data in the environment's order).

checks(gamma) lists what a trained module must output: per agent and state, the expected value (per agent; the grouped paradigms' value is the sum over the agents, as their reward is) and/or the expected action mean.

def __init__(self, env_config: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None:
    super().__init__()
    config = env_config or {}
    n = int(config.get("n_agents", 3))
    if config.get("scramble_ids"):
        # e.g. agent_2, agent_10, agent_1: sorted is agent_1, agent_10, agent_2
        numbers = [2, 10, 1] + list(range(11, 8 + n))
        self.agents_id = [f"agent_{k}" for k in numbers[:n]]
    else:
        self.agents_id = [f"agent_{k:02d}" for k in range(n)]
    self.agents = self.possible_agents = list(self.agents_id)
    box = spaces.Box(-1.0, 1.0, (1,), np.float32)
    self.observation_spaces = {a: box for a in self.agents_id}
    self.action_spaces = {a: box for a in self.agents_id}
    self.rng = np.random.default_rng(config.get("seed"))
    self.t = 0
    # Targets for the action probes: one per agent, all different.
    self.targets = {
        a: float(t) for a, t in zip(self.agents_id, np.linspace(-0.6, 0.6, n))
    }

core.rl.envs.shapes · source on GitHub

A synthetic environment with the market's shapes, for timing the learner.

Each agent observes as many numbers and sends as many actions as a MARLEM market agent (obs_dim 42, act_dim 4; with partner preference the observation also holds one reputation per agent, 42 + n_agents), in episodes of the market's length (24 hourly steps by default). Nothing else of the market is in it: observations are drawn at random every step and the reward is cheap, so a run on it times RLlib and the networks alone. The market's own cost per step is measured on the market side (notebooks/market/benchmark_market_step.ipynb).

The reward is learnable, so the same runs also show whether a paradigm still learns at this size: each agent has a fixed random linear target t_i = clip(W_i o_i, -1, 1) and gets 1 - mean((a_i - t_i)^2) per step: about 0.2 for an untrained policy (wide Gaussian actions), at most about 0.7 for one that ignores its observation (always 0), and 1 for the right one.

Source code in core\rl\envs\shapes.py 
def step(self, action_dict: dict[str, np.ndarray]):
    rewards = {}
    for a in self.agents_id:
        action = np.clip(np.asarray(action_dict[a], np.float32), -1.0, 1.0)
        target = np.clip(self.weights[a] @ self.obs[a], -1.0, 1.0)
        rewards[a] = float(1.0 - np.mean((action - target) ** 2))
    self.t += 1
    done = self.t >= self.length
    self._draw()
    terminateds = {a: done for a in self.agents_id} | {"__all__": done}
    truncateds = {a: False for a in self.agents_id} | {"__all__": False}
    return dict(self.obs), rewards, terminateds, truncateds, {}

docs.text:
core.rl.envs.spread · source on GitHub

Farama MPE2 simple_spread as an environment the trainer can use.

A second test of the RL code after the probes (core/rl/envs/probes.py): a standard cooperative multi-agent task with continuous actions, small enough to train in minutes and to watch (notebooks/rl/simple_spread.ipynb).

The task: n_agents agents and as many landmarks in a 2D plane. The agents should cover the landmarks, one each, without bumping into each other. Episodes last max_cycles steps (25) and end by time, never by success.

  • Observation (Box(-inf, inf, (6 * n_agents,)) per agent): own velocity (2), own position (2), the position of each landmark relative to the agent (2 each), the position of each other agent relative to the agent (2 each) and the other agents' communication (2 each, always 0: the agents are silent). 18 numbers for 3 agents.
  • Action (Box(0, 1, (5,)) per agent, as in PettingZoo's MPE with continuous actions): [no-op, left, right, down, up]. The agent is pushed with the force (right - left, up - down) (times 5); element 0 is not used. So the action [0, 0, 0, 0, 0] is "no force" and [x, 1, 1, 0, 0] also is: left and right cancel. Values are clipped to [0, 1] here.
  • Reward (per agent): local_ratio times the agent's own reward (minus one for each other agent it touches) plus 1 - local_ratio times the team's reward (minus the distance from each landmark to the nearest agent, summed over the landmarks). The team part is the same for everyone, so the task is cooperative. The sum over the agents is the episode return RLlib reports.

The interface is that of core/rl/envs/toy.py: built as SimpleSpread(env_config), fixed agents_id (agent_00, agent_01, ..., zero-padded so that sorted order, which GroupedEnv uses, equals this order), one Box per agent in observation_spaces and action_spaces, and "__all__" in terminateds and truncateds. PettingZoo ends the episode by truncation at max_cycles; that is passed on as truncateds, with terminateds always False.

def step(self, action_dict: dict[str, np.ndarray]):
    actions = {
        self._pz[a]: np.clip(np.asarray(action_dict[a], dtype=np.float32), 0.0, 1.0)
        for a in self.agents_id

    # observation of an ended episode is still returned.
    done = any(terminations.values())
    cut = any(truncations.values()) and not done

def baseline_return(
    env_config: dict[str, Any],
    policy: str,
    episodes: int = 200,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> float:
    """Mean episode return of all agents together (what RLlib reports as
    ``episode_return_mean``) under ``policy``: ``"random"`` (each action element
    uniform in [0, 1]) or ``"zero"`` (the no-op action, all zeros: no force)."""
    env = SimpleSpread({**env_config, "render_mode": None})
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    totals = []
    for episode in range(episodes):
        env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        total, done = 0.0, False
        while not done:
            if policy == "random":
                actions = {
                    a: rng.uniform(0, 1, env.action_spaces[a].shape).astype(np.float32)
                    for a in env.agents_id
                }
            elif policy == "zero":
                actions = {
                    a: np.zeros(env.action_spaces[a].shape, dtype=np.float32)
                    for a in env.agents_id
                }
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown policy {policy!r}")
            _, rewards, terminateds, truncateds, _ = env.step(actions)
            total += sum(rewards.values())
            done = terminateds["__all__"] or truncateds["__all__"]
        totals.append(total)
    env.close()
    return float(np.mean(totals))

def episode_frames(
    env_config: dict[str, Any],
    act: Callable[[dict[str, np.ndarray]], dict[str, np.ndarray]],
    seed: int = 0,
    size: int = 240,
) -> tuple[list[np.ndarray], float]:
    """Play one episode, drawing every step.

    Args:
        env_config: As for ``SimpleSpread`` (``render_mode`` is set here).
        act: Maps all agents' observations to all agents' actions.
        seed: Seed of the episode, so two policies can start from the same state.
        size: Frame width and height in pixels (the environment draws 700).

    Returns:
        The frames (the start and the state after each step, RGB, ``size`` x
        ``size``) and the episode return summed over the agents.
    """
    from PIL import Image

    env = SimpleSpread({**env_config, "render_mode": "rgb_array"})

    def frame() -> np.ndarray:
        image = Image.fromarray(env.render()).resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS)
        return np.asarray(image)

    obs, _ = env.reset(seed=seed)
    frames, total, done = [frame()], 0.0, False
    while not done:
        obs, rewards, terminateds, truncateds, _ = env.step(act(obs))
        frames.append(frame())
        total += sum(rewards.values())
        done = terminateds["__all__"] or truncateds["__all__"]
    env.close()
    return frames, total

def random_policy(env_config: dict[str, Any], seed: int = 0):
    """A policy for ``episode_frames``: every action element uniform in [0, 1]."""

        a: rng.uniform(0, 1, shape[a].shape).astype(np.float32) for a in obs
    }

core.rl.envs.toy · source on GitHub

Small multi-agent environments with a known best return, for testing the RL code.

They have the interface the trainer needs from the local energy market (core/rl/train.py), so the algorithms and training paradigms can be checked without it:

  • built as Env(env_config);
  • agents_id: the agents, in a fixed order;
  • observation_spaces and action_spaces: one Box per agent;
  • reset and step return one entry per agent, and "__all__" in terminateds and truncateds; an episode lasts max_steps steps.

Two tasks, each with a known best and random return per agent and episode:

  • TargetEnv: each agent sees a private target and is paid for matching it. Rewards are individual, so every paradigm should learn it.
  • BalanceEnv: each agent sees its own net position and chooses a trade; all agents get the same team reward for the total imbalance. The best policy is still "trade your own position", but each agent's effect on its reward is mixed with everyone else's (credit assignment), which centralised training should handle better than independent learners.

def baseline_return(
    env_class: type[_ToyEnv],
    env_config: dict[str, Any],
    policy: str,
    episodes: int = 200,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> float:
    """Mean episode return of all agents together (what RLlib reports as
    ``episode_return_mean``) under ``policy``: ``"best"``, ``"random"`` or
    ``"zero"`` (always act 0)."""
    env = env_class(env_config)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    totals = []
    for episode in range(episodes):
        env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        total, done = 0.0, False
        while not done:
            if policy == "best":
                actions = {a: env.best_action(a) for a in env.agents_id}
            elif policy == "random":
                actions = {
                    a: rng.uniform(-1, 1, env.act_dim).astype(np.float32)
                    for a in env.agents_id
                }
            elif policy == "zero":
                actions = {
                    a: np.zeros(env.act_dim, dtype=np.float32) for a in env.agents_id
                }
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown policy {policy!r}")
            _, rewards, terminateds, _, _ = env.step(actions)
            total += sum(rewards.values())
            done = terminateds["__all__"]
        totals.append(total)
    return float(np.mean(totals))

core.rl.benchmark · source on GitHub

Time one algorithm and paradigm at one problem size.

Not a training run: no evaluation, no checkpoint. It builds the configuration build_config would train with, then measures, in this order:

build     building the algorithm (networks, optimisers, the sampler)
warm-up   iterations until the learner has reported its first update
          (PPO: one batch; SAC: ``num_steps_sampled_before_learning_starts``;
          APPO: its first report, which can come thousands of steps after
          its first update) and at least ``warmup_iterations``; not counted
          below
timed     iterations until ``timed_env_steps`` environment steps (or
          ``max_seconds``): seconds per 1000 environment steps, gradient
          steps, samples trained
sampling  the same sampler alone, ``sample_env_steps`` steps with the
          current policy and no learning: what acting costs; the rest of
          the timed phase is learning

Every setting that decides the cost is written out in the record (batch, minibatch, epochs, warm-up, replay), with RLlib's defaults filled in, so a result says exactly what was measured.

def settings(config, algorithm: Algorithm) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The settings that decide the cost of an iteration, defaults filled in."""
    out = {
        "train_batch_size_per_learner": config.train_batch_size_per_learner,
        "rollout_fragment_length": config.get_rollout_fragment_length(),
        "fcnet_hiddens": config.model_config.get("fcnet_hiddens"),
    }
    if algorithm == Algorithm.SAC:
        out |= {
            "num_steps_sampled_before_learning_starts": (
                config.num_steps_sampled_before_learning_starts
            ),
            "training_intensity": config.training_intensity,
            "replay_capacity": config.replay_buffer_config.get("capacity"),
            "actor_lr": config.actor_lr,
            "critic_lr": config.critic_lr,
        }
    else:
        out |= {
            "minibatch_size": config.minibatch_size,
            "num_epochs": config.num_epochs,
            "lr": config.lr,
        }
    return out

def benchmark(bench: Bench) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run one benchmark (see the module docstring) and return its record."""
    algorithm, paradigm = Algorithm(bench.algorithm), Paradigm(bench.paradigm)
    env = bench.env_class(bench.env_config)
    n_agents = len(env.agents_id)
    episode_length = getattr(env, "length", None)
    config = build_config(
        algorithm,
        paradigm,
        bench.env_class,
        bench.env_config,
        seed=bench.seed,
        training=bench.training,
        num_gpus=bench.num_gpus,
        model=bench.model,
    )
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "algorithm": algorithm.value,
        "paradigm": paradigm.value,
        "device": "gpu" if bench.num_gpus else "cpu",
        "n_agents": n_agents,
        "agent_obs_dim": int(env.observation_spaces[env.agents_id[0]].shape[0]),
        "agent_act_dim": int(env.action_spaces[env.agents_id[0]].shape[0]),
        "episode_length": episode_length,
        "env_config": bench.env_config,
        "settings": settings(config, algorithm),
        "gradient_batch": gradient_batch(config, algorithm),
        "torch_threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
        "git": _git(),
        "started": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "status": "running",
    }
    _write(bench.out, record)

    started_ray = not ray.is_initialized()
    if started_ray:
        ray.init(num_cpus=1, num_gpus=bench.num_gpus, include_dashboard=False)
    algo = None
    try:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        algo = config.build_algo()
        record["build_s"] = time.perf_counter() - start
        record |= _shapes(algo)

        # Warm-up: until the learner has updated once, and warmup_iterations.
        start, iterations, trained = time.perf_counter(), 0, 0
        while iterations < bench.warmup_iterations or trained == 0:
            steps, trained, _ = _counters(algo.train())
            iterations += 1
            if time.perf_counter() - start > bench.max_seconds:
                raise TimeoutError(f"no learner update after {steps} env steps")
        record["warmup"] = {
            "iterations": iterations,
            "env_steps": steps,
            "seconds": time.perf_counter() - start,
        }

        # Timed: whole iterations, until timed_env_steps or max_seconds.
        steps0, trained0, return0 = steps, trained, None
        start, iterations = time.perf_counter(), 0
        while True:
            steps, trained, team_return = _counters(algo.train())
            iterations += 1
            return0 = team_return if return0 is None else return0
            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
            if steps - steps0 >= bench.timed_env_steps or elapsed > bench.max_seconds:
                break
        env_steps, samples = steps - steps0, trained - trained0
        # APPO's learner reports its counters only now and then: no count then.
        grad_steps = samples / record["gradient_batch"] if samples else math.nan
        record["timed"] = {
            "iterations": iterations,
            "env_steps": env_steps,
            "seconds": elapsed,
            "samples_trained": samples,
            "gradient_steps": grad_steps,
        }

        # Sampling alone: the same sampler, current policy, no learning.
        start = time.perf_counter()
        algo.env_runner.sample(num_timesteps=bench.sample_env_steps, explore=True)
        sample_s = time.perf_counter() - start

        per_1k = 1000 * elapsed / env_steps
        sample_per_1k = 1000 * sample_s / bench.sample_env_steps
        reward_scale = n_agents * (episode_length or 1)
        record["results"] = {
            "s_per_1k_env_steps": per_1k,
            "sample_s_per_1k": sample_per_1k,
            "learn_s_per_1k": max(per_1k - sample_per_1k, 0.0),
            "env_steps_per_s": env_steps / elapsed,
            "gradient_steps_per_s": grad_steps / elapsed,
            "gradient_steps_per_1k_env_steps": 1000 * grad_steps / env_steps,
            "h_per_1M_env_steps": per_1k * 1000 / 3600,
            "reward_per_agent_step_start": return0 / reward_scale,
            "reward_per_agent_step_end": team_return / reward_scale,
            "rss_gb": psutil.Process(os.getpid()).memory_info().rss / 1e9,
            "gpu_peak_gb": (
                torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1e9 if bench.num_gpus else 0.0
            ),
        }
        record["status"] = "completed"
    except Exception as error:
        record |= {"status": "failed", "error": repr(error)}
    finally:
        record["finished"] = datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
        _write(bench.out, record)
        if algo is not None:
            algo.stop()
        if started_ray:
            ray.shutdown()
    return record

docs.title: config
docs.text:
core.rl.config · source on GitHub

The algorithm configuration of one combination of algorithm and paradigm.

Only RLlib's algorithms and modules are used; what changes between paradigms is the environment the algorithm sees and, for CTDE, what the actor reads:

Paradigm Environment Modules Objective DTDE the multi-agent environment one per agent, RLlib's default own reward CTDE CentralStateEnv: o_i plus the global state one per agent, actor on o_i, critic on everything (ctde_modules.py) own reward CTCE GroupedEnv: one agent, joint Box spaces one, RLlib's default summed reward (social planner)

DTDE and CTDE optimise the same individual objective and differ only in what the critic sees, so a difference between them is the central critic's.

Every paradigm uses the same network settings (RLlib's defaults: 2 x 256 tanh, separate actor and critic), which fixes R-03.

The hyperparameters start from the original's (SETTINGS, [P2] Table 8), with the defects removed:

  • PPO: use_kl_loss=False, so the KL term is not computed at all (fixes R-02; the original set kl_coeff=0 and kept it). vf_clip_param raised from RLlib's 10: RLlib caps the squared value error there, so an error above about 3.2 would give the critic no gradient at all. Rewards should still be scaled by the environment to returns of order 1-10.
  • APPO: no lambda_; RLlib's V-trace has no lambda (fixes R-06).
  • SAC: target_entropy="auto" (the negative action size of each module: the agent's in DTDE and CTDE, the group's in CTCE, as the original intended), a uniform replay buffer of 1000 steps for every paradigm. Episodes are sampled in fragments (RLlib's default), not complete_episodes as in the original: in that mode RLlib 2.51 resets the environment with the run's seed at every sample call, so with a seed every SAC training step would replay the same episode.
  • No population-based training and no Ray Tune (fixes I-49 and part of I-62): one run has fixed hyperparameters and one seed; tuning and seeds are loops around core/rl/train.py.
  • Iterations are not tied to wall-clock time (min_time_s_per_iteration=0), and the budget is counted in environment steps by the trainer (fixes I-50).

def env_spec(
    paradigm: Paradigm, env_class: type, env_config: dict
) -> tuple[type, dict, list[str]]:
    """The environment the algorithm trains on, its config, and its agent ids."""
    if paradigm == Paradigm.DTDE:
        env = env_class(env_config)
        return env_class, env_config, list(env.agents_id)
    wrapped = {"env_class": env_class, "env_config": env_config}
    if paradigm == Paradigm.CTDE:
        return CentralStateEnv, wrapped, list(env_class(env_config).agents_id)
    return GroupedEnv, wrapped, [GROUP]

        env_config: Its config.
        seed: Seed of RLlib (network initialisation, sampling, environment seeds).
        training: Overrides of ``SETTINGS``, passed to ``AlgorithmConfig.training``
            (e.g. ``lr=3e-4``, ``train_batch_size_per_learner=1000``).
        num_env_runners: Sampling processes besides the driver (0: sample in the
            driver). Learning always runs in the driver; nothing else starts
            processes (fixes the doubled CPU count of I-62).
        num_gpus: GPUs for the learner (0 or 1).
        model: Overrides of the network settings ``MODEL`` (the same for every
            paradigm).
    """
    algorithm, paradigm = Algorithm(algorithm), Paradigm(paradigm)
    env_config = dict(env_config or {})
    env, config_for_env, module_ids = env_spec(paradigm, env_class, env_config)
    model_config = MODEL | (model or {})

    config = (
        CONFIGS[algorithm]()
        .framework("torch")
        .environment(env=env, env_config=config_for_env)
        .env_runners(num_env_runners=num_env_runners, sample_timeout_s=None)
        .learners(num_learners=0, num_gpus_per_learner=num_gpus)
        .training(**(SETTINGS[algorithm] | (training or {})))
        .reporting(min_time_s_per_iteration=0)
        .debugging(seed=seed)
        .multi_agent(
            policies=set(module_ids),
            policy_mapping_fn=lambda agent_id, episode, **kwargs: agent_id,
        )
    )
    # The algorithm adds its own keys (e.g. SAC's twin_q) to config.model_config.
    config = config.rl_module(model_config=model_config)

    if paradigm == Paradigm.CTDE:
        central = CentralStateEnv(config_for_env)
        specs = {
            mid: RLModuleSpec(
                module_class=CTDE_MODULES[algorithm.value],
                model_config=config.model_config
                | {"own_obs_dim": central.own_dims[mid]},
            )
            for mid in module_ids
        }
    else:
        specs = {mid: RLModuleSpec() for mid in module_ids}
    return config.rl_module(rl_module_spec=MultiRLModuleSpec(rl_module_specs=specs))

docs.text:
core.rl.ctde_modules · source on GitHub

CTDE modules: RLlib's own modules with a decentralised actor and a central critic.

CTDE here is MAPPO / MASAC with one module per agent (no parameter sharing): each agent keeps its own reward, its own critic and its own PPO clip or SAC temperature, exactly as in DTDE. The only difference from DTDE is what the networks see. Under CentralStateEnv (grouping.py) agent i observes [o_i, o_1, ..., o_N]:

  • the actor reads only o_i, the first own_obs_dim entries, so the agent can act on its own observation after training (decentralised execution);
  • the critic reads all of it, its own observation and the global state (centralised training): V_i(s) for PPO and APPO, Q_i(s, a_i) for SAC.

Each module is RLlib's default PPO, APPO or SAC module, with one change: the actor's encoder is replaced by the encoder RLlib's catalog builds for the agent's own observation, applied to its slice. The policy head, the critic, the losses, rsample, target networks, log-std clipping and tanh squashing stay RLlib's.

Fixes I-48 (the networks the loss trains are the networks that act) and the deviations from standard multi-agent PPO of the earlier grouped CTDE: rewards, advantages and the PPO clip are per agent. Known deviation from MADDPG / MASAC: the SAC critic Q_i(s, a_i) does not take the other agents' actions.

model_config keys (besides RLlib's): own_obs_dim, the size of the agent's own observation.

def own_encoder(module) -> OwnObsEncoder:
    """The encoder RLlib builds for the agent's own observation, on its slice."""
    dim = int(module.model_config["own_obs_dim"])
    space = module.observation_space
    if not isinstance(space, spaces.Box) or len(space.shape) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"CTDE needs a flat Box observation space, got {space}.")
    own = spaces.Box(space.low[:dim], space.high[:dim], dtype=space.dtype)
    catalog = type(module.catalog)(own, module.action_space, dict(module.model_config))
    if hasattr(catalog, "actor_critic_encoder_config"):  # PPO, APPO
        encoder = catalog.actor_critic_encoder_config.base_encoder_config.build(
            framework="torch"
        )
    else:  # SAC
        encoder = catalog.build_encoder(framework="torch")
    return OwnObsEncoder(encoder, dim)

docs.title: grouping
docs.text:
core.rl.grouping · source on GitHub

How the paradigms see a multi-agent environment: grouped (CTCE) or with a central state (CTDE).

GroupedEnv (CTCE): all agents as one agent, "group". It observes every agent's observation and outputs every agent's action, each joined into one flat Box in the environment's agent order, and receives the sum of the agents' rewards: one controller maximising the total (the social planner). RLlib's own modules and algorithms train it as an ordinary single agent.

CentralStateEnv (CTDE): the agents stay separate, each with its own reward, but each agent's observation is extended with the global state, every agent's observation joined: [o_i, o_1, ..., o_N]. The CTDE modules (core/rl/ctde_modules.py) let the actor read only o_i and the critic read all of it, so the critic is central and the actor decentralised.

Fixes I-59: the original put the agents' spaces in sorted name order and their data in environment order. Here both follow env.agents_id, and each agent keeps its own action bounds in its slice of the joint Box, so RLlib rescales every agent's action to that agent's bounds.

def step(
    self, action_dict: MultiAgentDict
) -> tuple[
    MultiAgentDict, MultiAgentDict, MultiAgentDict, MultiAgentDict, MultiAgentDict
]:
    actions = split(action_dict[GROUP], self.agents_id, self.act_dims)
    obs, rewards, terminateds, truncateds, infos = self.env.step(actions)
    missing = set(self.agents_id) - set(rewards)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"GroupedEnv needs every agent at every step; no reward for {missing}."
        )
    group_reward = float(sum(rewards[a] for a in self.agents_id))
    return (
        {GROUP: join(obs, self.agents_id)},
        {GROUP: group_reward},
        {GROUP: terminateds["__all__"], "__all__": terminateds["__all__"]},
        {GROUP: truncateds["__all__"], "__all__": truncateds["__all__"]},
        {GROUP: {"rewards": dict(rewards), "infos": infos}},
    )

def split_space(box: spaces.Box, dims: list[int]) -> list[spaces.Box]:
    """Cut a joint ``Box`` back into one ``Box`` per agent."""
    edges = np.cumsum([0, *dims])
    return [
        spaces.Box(box.low[a:b], box.high[a:b], dtype=np.float32)
        for a, b in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:])
    ]

def split(joint: np.ndarray, agents: list[str], dims: list[int]) -> dict:
    """Cut a joint vector into each agent's part, in ``agents`` order."""
    edges = np.cumsum([0, *dims])
    return {
        agent: np.asarray(joint[..., a:b], dtype=np.float32)
        for agent, a, b in zip(agents, edges[:-1], edges[1:])
    }

core.rl.policy · source on GitHub

Acting with a trained module, baselines, and evaluation on held-out seeds.

One evaluation for every paradigm: episodes run in the original multi-agent environment (never the grouped one), and returns are computed from its raw per-agent rewards, so all nine combinations and the baselines are scored the same way.

  • Fixes I-61: a Policy acts as RLlib does in training: the module's action distribution, then RLlib's own unsquash_action from [-1, 1] to each agent's bounds. Infos are returned per agent, as the environment gives them.
  • Fixes I-73: the team score is the sum over agents of the episode return, from the raw rewards; per-agent returns are reported next to it.
  • Fixes I-64 and I-72 (the capability): random, constant and untrained policies on the same seeds, and evaluation seeds that training never uses.

def act(self, obs: dict, explore: bool = False) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Each agent's action, in the environment's units.

    Args:
        obs: Each agent's observation.
        explore: Sample from the policy (as in training) instead of taking its
            most likely action.
    """
    unit = self._unit_actions(obs, explore)
    if self.paradigm != Paradigm.CTCE:
        return {
            a: np.asarray(unsquash_action(unit[a], self.act_spaces[a]), np.float32)
            for a in self.agents
        }
    joint = np.asarray(unsquash_action(unit[GROUP], self.joint_space), np.float32)
    return split(joint, self.agents, self.act_dims)

def values(self, obs: dict) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Each module's value of the state: ``V`` (PPO, APPO) or, for SAC, the
    smaller twin ``Q`` at the policy's most likely action: per agent in DTDE and
    CTDE (each agent's own return), the group's in CTCE (the summed return)."""
    unit = self._unit_actions(obs, explore=False)
    out = {}
    with torch.no_grad():
        for mid, x in self._inputs(obs).items():
            module = self.modules[mid]
            batch = {Columns.OBS: torch.as_tensor(x).reshape(1, -1)}
            if isinstance(module, ValueFunctionAPI):
                out[mid] = float(module.compute_values(batch)[0])
            else:
                batch[Columns.ACTIONS] = torch.as_tensor(unit[mid]).reshape(1, -1)
                out[mid] = float(module.compute_q_values(batch)[0])
    return out

def random_policy(env, seed: int = 0) -> ActFn:
    """Uniform random actions within each agent's bounds."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    def act(obs):
        return {
            a: rng.uniform(env.action_spaces[a].low, env.action_spaces[a].high).astype(
                np.float32
            )
            for a in env.agents_id
        }

    return act

def constant_policy(env, value: float = 0.0) -> ActFn:
    """The same action ``value`` for every agent and dimension, within bounds."""

    def act(obs):
        return {
            a: np.clip(
                np.full(env.action_spaces[a].shape, value, dtype=np.float32),
                env.action_spaces[a].low,
                env.action_spaces[a].high,
            )
            for a in env.agents_id
        }

    return act

def rollout(
    env_class: type,
    env_config: dict,
    act: ActFn,
    seeds: list[int],
    max_steps: int = 100_000,
) -> list[Episode]:
    """Run one episode per seed with ``act`` in the multi-agent environment."""
    env = env_class(env_config)
    episodes = []
    for seed in seeds:
        obs, infos = env.reset(seed=int(seed))
        episode = Episode(seed=int(seed), infos=[infos])
        for _ in range(max_steps):
            obs, rewards, terminateds, truncateds, infos = env.step(act(obs))
            episode.rewards.append({a: float(r) for a, r in rewards.items()})
            episode.infos.append(infos)
            if terminateds["__all__"] or truncateds["__all__"]:
                break
        episodes.append(episode)
    return episodes

def summarize(episodes: list[Episode]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Mean and spread of the team score, and each agent's mean return."""
    team = np.array([e.team_return() for e in episodes])
    returns = [e.returns() for e in episodes]
    per_agent = {a: float(np.mean([r[a] for r in returns])) for a in returns[0]}
    return {
        "team_return_mean": float(team.mean()),
        "team_return_std": float(team.std()),
        "episodes": len(episodes),
        **{f"return/{a}": float(v) for a, v in per_agent.items()},
    }

def evaluate(
    env_class: type,
    env_config: dict,
    policies: dict[str, ActFn],
    seeds: list[int],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score several policies on the same seeds; one row per policy."""
    rows = []
    for name, act in policies.items():
        row = summarize(rollout(env_class, env_config, act, seeds))
        rows.append({"policy": name, **row})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def evaluation_seeds(n: int, start: int = 1_000_000) -> list[int]:
    """Seeds for evaluation episodes. Training resets with RLlib's run seed only
    once per sampler and lets the environment's generator run on, so seeds from
    ``start`` on are episodes training has not seen."""
    return list(range(start, start + n))

def baselines(env_class: type, env_config: dict, seed: int = 0) -> dict[str, ActFn]:

docs.title: train
docs.text:
core.rl.train · source on GitHub

Train one run, record it, and load its policy again.

A run is one algorithm, one paradigm, one seed and one budget of environment steps. Everything around it is written to the run's folder:

run.json         what was run: settings, environment, seed, versions, git
                 commit, status, final scores (fixes I-64's missing record)
metrics.csv      one row per training iteration: environment steps, team
                 return, the learner's losses, entropy, KL, ...
evaluation.csv   the policy and the baselines on held-out seeds, at fixed
                 environment-step counts (fixes I-64's missing baselines)
checkpoint/      the algorithm at the end of the budget

What it fixes:

  • I-50: the budget is counted in environment steps, the same for every algorithm and paradigm; iterations are only how often metrics are written.
  • R-02: training stops with an error as soon as a loss or metric is NaN or infinite, instead of zeroing the gradients and continuing.
  • I-62: no evaluation workers, no doubled CPU count, no population-based training; the algorithm is stopped and Ray shut down even when a run fails.
  • I-61: load_policy acts with the trained module exactly as training does (core/rl/policy.py).

def train(run: Run) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Train one run and write its record (see the module docstring).

    Returns:
        The run record, as in ``run.json``.
    """
    out = (
        Path(run.out_dir)
        if run.out_dir
        else (
            REPO / "runs" / f"{run.algorithm}_{run.paradigm}_seed{run.seed}_"
            f"{datetime.now():%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}"
        )
    )
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    config = build_config(
        run.algorithm,
        run.paradigm,
        run.env_class,
        run.env_config,
        seed=run.seed,
        training=run.training,
        num_env_runners=run.num_env_runners,
        num_gpus=run.num_gpus,
        model=run.model,
    )
    record = _record(run, config) | {"out_dir": str(out)}
    _write_json(out / "run.json", record)

    started_ray = not ray.is_initialized()
    if started_ray:
        ray.init(
            num_cpus=run.num_env_runners + 1,
            num_gpus=run.num_gpus,
            include_dashboard=False,
        )
    algo, start = None, time.time()
    rows, evaluations = [], []
    seeds = evaluation_seeds(run.eval_episodes)
    env = run.env_class(run.env_config)

    def evaluate_now(env_steps: int, extra: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
        policies = {"trained": Policy(learner_modules(algo), run.paradigm, env)}
        frame = evaluate(run.env_class, run.env_config, policies | (extra or {}), seeds)
        frame.insert(0, "env_steps", env_steps)
        evaluations.append(frame)
        pd.concat(evaluations).to_csv(out / "evaluation.csv", index=False)

    try:
        algo = config.build_algo()
        # Step 0: the untrained policy and the baselines, on the same seeds.
        evaluate_now(0, baselines(run.env_class, run.env_config, run.seed))
        env_steps, iteration = 0, 0
        next_eval = run.eval_every or run.budget
        while env_steps < run.budget:
            result = algo.train()
            iteration += 1
            row = _iteration_row(iteration, result)
            env_steps = row["env_steps"]
            rows.append(row)
            pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(out / "metrics.csv", index=False)
            bad = _nonfinite(result.get(LEARNER_RESULTS, {}))
            if bad:
                raise FloatingPointError(
                    f"Non-finite learner metrics at iteration {iteration} "
                    f"({env_steps} env steps): {', '.join(bad[:10])}"
                )
            if env_steps >= next_eval and env_steps < run.budget:
                evaluate_now(env_steps)
                next_eval += run.eval_every
        evaluate_now(env_steps)
        algo.save_to_path(str((out / "checkpoint").resolve()))
        final = evaluations[-1].set_index("policy").loc["trained"].to_dict()
        record |= {
            "status": "completed",
            "env_steps": env_steps,
            "iterations": iteration,
            "final": final,
        }
    except Exception as error:
        record |= {
            "status": "failed",
            "error": repr(error),
            "traceback": traceback.format_exc(),
        }
        raise
    finally:
        record["duration_s"] = round(time.time() - start, 1)
        record["finished"] = datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
        _write_json(out / "run.json", record)
        if algo is not None:
            algo.stop()
        if started_ray:
            ray.shutdown()
    return record

def load_policy(run_dir: str | Path) -> tuple[Policy, dict[str, Any]]:
    """The trained policy of a finished run, and its record.

    The policy acts in the run's multi-agent environment as in training; no
    algorithm or Ray is needed.
    """
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    record = json.loads((run_dir / "run.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    env_class = _load_class(record["env_class"])
    with _checkpoint_imports():
        modules = MultiRLModule.from_checkpoint(
            str(
                (
                    run_dir
                    / "checkpoint"
                    / COMPONENT_LEARNER_GROUP
                    / COMPONENT_LEARNER
                    / COMPONENT_RL_MODULE
                ).resolve()
            )
        )
    env = env_class(record["env_config"])
    return Policy(modules, record["paradigm"], env), record
